tagline: The town where soldiers found a press and printed a paper.
intro: The byway is a few miles of Routes 25 and AA around Bloomfield, the Stoddard County seat, 6.5 miles north of Dexter on Route 25. The town was platted in 1835 and named for the wildflowers around it.

In November 1861 Union troops marched in under orders to catch the Missouri State Guard general M. Jeff Thompson, the Swamp Fox, and found the town abandoned. Ten of the soldiers were printers by trade. With their colonel's permission they took over the local press, and the first Stars and Stripes came off it. Then the paper went quiet for 57 years, until General Pershing revived it in France in 1918.

moments.title: Stoddard County Courthouse
moments.text: The two-story brick courthouse, built between 1867 and 1870 and remodeled in Classical Revival style in 1909, carries a massive clock tower on its roof.

moments.title: Stars and Stripes National Museum and Library
moments.text: The museum in the paper's birthplace keeps the first edition among more than 20,000 artifacts, and Barney, its cat since 2018, greets visitors in the gift shop.
